source.title: On Effects of Steering Latent Representation for Large Language Model Unlearning
source.authors: Dang Huu-Tien; Trung-Tin Pham; Hoang Thanh-Tung; Naoya Inoue

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates RMU using WMDP question-answer accuracy and general-knowledge performance, and varies the unlearning layer. It does not empirically test knowledge-recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper's own RMU and Adaptive RMU accuracy results are recorded. Its theoretical discussion of GCG robustness is not an applied jailbreak result; the GCG experiment it mentions is attributed to Li et al. The MaxLogit finding is recorded under fits_no_version because confidence is not one of the claim versions' recovery measures.
record.test_reason: The study runs RMU, and its own Adaptive RMU, on WMDP-Bio/Cyber with MMLU as the utility check, the same method and measure as the WMDP original. It reports targeted accuracy against base across models, layers and retain sets. It runs no recovery attack (fine-tuning, ablation, quantization or prompting). Its GCG robustness claim is a theoretical argument that leans on Li et al.'s experiment. So only the unlearning-efficacy part of A is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors argue that steering forget representations to a random vector lowers token confidence, and that RMU fails at middle and late layers because the forget loss does not converge when the representation norm exceeds c. They propose Adaptive RMU, which they call state of the art on WMDP with retained MMLU. They also assert that RMU models are robust to jailbreaks, but they support this only with a theoretical gradient argument and Li et al.'s prior GCG result, not an attack of their own.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates RMU as the baseline, using c = 6.5 and WMDP tasks, and studies different unlearning layers. It also proposes Adaptive RMU, which scales the target using the frozen representation norm.
record.method_sensitivity: Unlearning layer changes outcomes: the paper reports RMU effective in early layers (3–10) and ineffective in middle/later layers (11–31). Adaptive RMU performance also varies by layer and by retain-set/task setting. Larger coefficient c is reported to increase WMDP accuracy reduction but to lower MMLU performance.

fits_no_version.finding: RMU Zephyr-7B (l=7) shows a narrower MaxLogit distribution, shifted to lower values, on WMDP prompts than the base model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RMU lowers generated-token confidence on forget-domain prompts; this does not show whether knowledge is deleted or recoverable.

fits_no_version.finding: A theoretical argument that RMU gives GCG near-zero, uninformative gradients, so white-box jailbreaks fail. No attack is run in this paper.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation-steering unlearning may resist gradient-based jailbreaks by flattening attacker gradients (untested argument).

record.problems: No error bars or uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper does not state a chance-level benchmark for its Q&A accuracies. The claimed GCG robustness is not empirically tested here, and the authors note experiments are mainly on 7B-sized or equivalent models and focus on white-box attack analysis.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within 60 rows, layer-specific Adaptive RMU results in Tables 2–4 are sampled at layers 5, 10, and 31; other layer entries in those tables are omitted. Table 6 is sampled at layers 6, 7, and 10; other layer entries are omitted. Figure 5's exact plotted values are not transcribed; the text-described RMU layer trend is recorded in r34–r35.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the knowledge. No attack is run; the GCG robustness claim is theoretical and cites Li et al.'s experiment.
Fine-tuning or relearning recovery is not tested.
Activation-direction ablation or block-versus-delete analysis is not tested. The noise-sensitivity and cosine analyses do not test recovery.
Rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery is not tested empirically.
Adaptive RMU is proposed but never evaluated against any recovery attack.

missing.what: Forget-task accuracies for MMLU-subset unlearning (e.g. layer 7: Econ 27.0, Law 26.4, Physics 23.8, against base 58.0/55.6/38.5)
Effect of coefficient c: larger c gives a larger WMDP drop but a significant MMLU drop (a trade-off with the hyperparameter)
Adaptive RMU Zephyr-7B layer sweep: average reductions of 13.1%/3.6% (early layers) and 15.6%/9.6% (middle/late layers) beyond RMU

record.verdict_notes: Every row's versions were the invalid label V1 and are relinked to A. The reader graded near-chance WMDP values as partial because no chance level was stated; WMDP is 4-choice, so about 25% is chance, and those rows are now observed. WMDP is an original source, but this paper is not, so verdicts are allowed. Table 1 values for LLMU, SCRUB and SSD are copied from Li et al. and correctly not rowed. Tranche is T1 for the efficacy measure only; the attack half of A and versions B–F are untested.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests targeted-task accuracy and general-knowledge performance, but does not apply attacks to see whether knowledge is recovered. It does not state a chance-level reference.
No fine-tuning recovery attack on an unlearned model.
No activation-direction ablation and no test of whether the targeted knowledge remains stored but inaccessible.
No empirical test of rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual, or in-context recovery.
Adaptive RMU is proposed and evaluated for unlearning performance, but is not tested against the recovery attacks in the claim.

source_check.notes: Plain RMU appears only on Zephyr (Table 1 l=7; Fig 5 sweep, figure-only). The Yi/Llama/Mistral tables are Adaptive RMU only, single runs, with no uncertainty or chance level stated. Adaptive RMU works at many middle layers on Yi/Mistral but fails at most layers of 10 and above on Llama. No empirical recovery attack: the robustness claim is a theoretical GCG argument plus a citation of Li et al.

statements.problem: The 24-29% figure with MMLU within 0-4 points holds only at selected early layers for each model, not across layers 3-10. Plain RMU is reported only on Zephyr; the Yi, Llama and Mistral tables are Adaptive RMU only.

statements.correction: Text: RMU (Zephyr, c=6.5) is effective at layers 3-10 and ineffective at 11-31. Adaptive RMU on Llama-3-8B: l=10 Bio 65.1, l=31 70.4 (base 71.2), Bio 59.6-65.2 at l=10-14. Adaptive RMU is near chance at middle layers on Yi (l=11-15 and 19: Bio 25.4-27.4) and Mistral (l=11, 15, 17: Bio 25.4-27.6). At layer 31: Yi 64.8 (base 64.8), Mistral 66.0 (base 67.3).
statements.problem: The numbers are right. But 'fail at 11-31' is the paper's finding for plain RMU on Zephyr (Fig 5). Adaptive RMU reaches near chance at several middle layers on Yi and Mistral. Llama l=10 (65.1) also falls inside the 3-10 range the same sentence says works. The Llama results are Adaptive RMU only.

statements.correction: Zephyr Adaptive RMU with WMDP retain sets (Table 6): l=6 Bio 28.1, MMLU 30.1; l=10 Bio 29.6, MMLU 29.3; l=7 Bio 62.6, MMLU 57.6. Table 5 subset unlearning at l=7: MMLU-Retain 58.9->39.4.

Adaptive RMU on Llama-3-8B, Bio (base 71.2): l=3 46.4, l=4 45.3, l=5 28.2, l=6 27.8, l=7 29.3, l=8 33.7, l=9 36.0, l=10 65.1, l=31 70.4. Plain RMU by layer is shown only for Zephyr (Fig 5; text: effective at 3-10, not at 11-31).
statements.problem: The Llama-3-8B results are Adaptive RMU only, so 'RMU/Adaptive RMU' attributes them to plain RMU, which the paper never runs on Llama. On Llama, 'early layers reach about chance' holds only at l=5-7.

statements.correction: Text: RMU (Zephyr, c=6.5) is effective at 3-10 and ineffective at 11-31. Adaptive RMU on Yi: l=11-15 and 19 Bio 25.4-27.4, with MMLU kept at l=13 (57.0 vs 60.0) and l=19 (56.7). On Mistral: l=11, 15, 17 Bio 25.4-27.6, with MMLU 56.7 at l=17 (base 58.7). On Llama-3-8B: l=10 Bio 65.1, l=31 70.4 (base 71.2). The Zephyr retain-set WMDP averages (26.0-28.4, 44.8, 43.54) are not from this study. This study's own in-domain result (Table 6) reaches chance only at l=6/10, with MMLU about 30.
statements.problem: 'RMU and Adaptive RMU ... fail at 11-31' fits plain RMU on Zephyr (text) and Adaptive RMU on Llama. It is wrong for Adaptive RMU on Yi and Mistral, which reach near chance at several middle layers. The Llama numbers are Adaptive RMU only.

statements.correction: Zephyr RMU l=7: Bio 28.8, Cyber 28.8, MMLU 56.8 (base 58.1). Adaptive RMU: Zephyr l=7 23.7/26.5; Yi l=7 26.1/25.5; Llama l=5 28.2/24.5; Mistral l=5 27.6/24.8, with MMLU within about 2-4 points. Not every early layer works (Yi l=8 Bio 63.3; Llama l=10 65.1). The paper runs no recovery attack, only a theoretical GCG argument.
statements.problem: 'RMU and Adaptive RMU at early layers reach about 24-29% on Zephyr, Yi-6B, Llama-3-8B and Mistral' holds only at selected early layers, and plain RMU is reported only on Zephyr.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Zephyr-7B-β, RMU and Adaptive RMU at layer 7, WMDP tasks and MMLU
reader_labels.reason: Target-task accuracies fall while MMLU remains near the Base value for RMU; Adaptive RMU also reduces WMDP accuracy, with a smaller MMLU decrease (r1–r6). Chance level is not stated, and the attack component of A is not tested.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Layer sweeps and in-domain retain-set or MMLU-subset settings
reader_labels.reason: RMU is reported ineffective at middle and later layers, some Adaptive RMU layer results are close to Base accuracy, and several settings substantially reduce general/retain-task accuracy (r13–r15, r19–r24, r31–r33, r35, r38–r47).
